title: How AI Learns to Look Things Up Before It Answers
subtitle: From memory to retrieval, GPUs, and edge devices
intro: NVIDIA just made seven industry-grade AI courses free. The big surprise is not that AI can write — it's that the smartest systems don't answer from memory alone, they look things up first.
takeaway: Modern AI works best when it retrieves fresh facts before it generates, runs fast on GPUs, and is checked for mistakes.

sections.heading: Analogy: Your AI is like a new intern with a library card
sections.body: Imagine a smart intern who memorized books until last year. From memory alone, answers are fast but outdated. Give that intern a library card to check your files first, and they quote the right page. That is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) — retrieval means fetching documents before generation, which means writing the answer.

sections.heading: Why it exists? Stop answering from memory alone
sections.body: Generative AI creates new text or images from a prompt. A Large Language Model (LLM) is a text predictor trained on huge data, but stuck in the past. RAG fixes this by connecting the LLM to fresh sources first. Video AI does this for video, and Edge AI on Jetson Nano — a tiny computer that runs AI on the device itself — brings it to the real world.

sections.heading: What can go wrong? When the helper makes things up
sections.body: What fails if many people ask at once? With messy files or no GPU — the chip that speeds up AI — answers get slow or false. Hallucination is when AI invents facts because retrieval failed. CUDA programming is code that runs fast on an NVIDIA GPU. Digital fingerprinting is a hidden mark that labels content as AI-made.

steps.narration: You ask, and the AI could guess from old memory.
RAG first pulls fresh pages from your documents.
The LLM then writes an answer using those pages.
CUDA lets a GPU run that work much faster.
Jetson Nano can run the result right on a small device.
Digital fingerprinting marks if the content was AI-made.

quiz.q: What does RAG add to a plain LLM?
options: It fetches your documents before writing
It makes video without a prompt
quiz.why: RAG = Retrieval-Augmented Generation: retrieve fresh context first, then generate.

quiz.q: What breaks first if your RAG system scales 100x with messy files and no GPU?
options: Jetson Nano makes its own data
quiz.why: Bad retrieval causes hallucinations, and without CUDA GPU acceleration, large loads get slow and fail.

options: To run code fast on NVIDIA GPUs
quiz.why: CUDA lets programs run in parallel on GPUs to accelerate AI.
